text: you think if we take the points of a wheel well, and then distance from the ground, to triangulate the exact center for tires to sit? also this worked btw so thanks.
resolution: Built the user's wheel-centre idea (find the exact tire centre from the wheel-well geometry) the clean way: instead of triangulating from arch points + ground distance, fit a CIRCLE to the arch verts — the circle centre is the axle and the radius is the tire size, with the ground distance falling out (centre height = radius when the tire rests on the ground). New pure fitWheelCenter(pts): a Kåsa algebraic least-squares circle fit performed in the well's plane (the flat/least-variance axis is taken as the well normal, the other two as the fit plane), mean-centred for conditioning, returns {center, radius, axis} or null for <3/collinear points. Studio: a '⌖ wheel center' button in vertex mode when 3+ verts are selected — fit the selection, drop a 'wheel' socket joint at the centre (mirror-aware: addMountReflections places both/all wheels when a mirror plane is on), switch to rig mode with the new joint selected, and toast the tire radius so the user sizes the wheel to match. Verified: editMesh suite 66/66 (synthetic arch recovers centre+radius; <3 and collinear return null), full hmsc-int cart bundles clean. Committed 2f577fd7f.
